analysis: This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/gptoss-decode-command-buffers.md, lines 1-3) and a docs/architecture/inference.md patch that bumps the 'Last updated' date and adds a 'GPT-OSS decode command buffers' section (head lines ~4816-4826). No executable source, key handling, attestation, WebSocket protocol, prefix-cache storage, or authorization code is changed in the supplied evidence. The docs describe a Metal command-buffer commit policy for GPT-OSS plain decode (every 100 operations, no input-size bound, via GPTOSSDecodeCommandBuffers / CBv2DecodeCommandBufferLimitsProviding) and claim bitwise-identical outputs and that prefill keeps MLX defaults. Relevant threat surfaces are TB-007 (inference engine), T-010 (cancellation/DoS), T-029 (GPU monopolisation) and T-028 (residual GPU data). None of their stated mitigations is altered in the supplied text, and the docs do not claim to change them. The underlying Swift implementation is not in this batch, so I cannot verify the claims about bitwise-identical outputs, whether removing the input-size bound affects memory pressure or in-flight command-buffer limits, or cancellation latency under the larger commit interval. These are performance/availability behaviours and not a demonstrated security regression. A later pass that sees the Swift change should check that fewer command-buffer commits do not delay cancellation (T-010) or memory release/clearing (T-028), and that the 'bitwise identical' claim is tested. No threat-model update appears necessary from the docs alone. The base excerpt of inference.md showed only unrelated pre-existing content around the change.
